children: No major changes in Israeli economic policy are expected irrespective of how the current political dynamics play out over the coming months, J.P. Morgan's strategists say. Israel's national legislative Knesset elections surprised last week with stronger results for both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's Arab parties. JPM forecasts two outcomes: an election re-run in 2027, which would be negative for risk assets, or a unity government, which would be more positive. "Increased market optimism and currency strength would imply wider room for the Bank of Israel to ease policy," the strategists say, adding there is less room for such an outcome since the vote. "We see a substantial risk that the last 25 basis points cut of the cycle, which we have penciled in for November, will never be delivered."(joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)
